summary: Describes the TLS cipher suites built on single DES and IDEA, which were defined for TLS 1.0 and 1.1 and dropped from TLS 1.2. It records them for completeness and explains why they should no longer be used. This document is historic and was replaced by RFC 8996.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 5469 documents TLS cipher suites that use single DES or IDEA and explains why they are no longer recommended. It says DES has only 56 bits of protection, while IDEA's TLS suite saw little use; RFC 8996 later obsoleted this memo.

subtitle: Why TLS cipher suites using single DES and IDEA are no longer recommended.

tldr.problem: TLS 1.0 and 1.1 defined cipher suites using DES and IDEA, but the RFC says single DES is vulnerable to brute-force attacks and the IDEA suite was rarely used.
tldr.mechanism: The memo records the cipher-suite definitions and explains why their use is no longer recommended.
tldr.outcome: RFC 5469 is Historic, was obsoleted by RFC 8996, and is updated by RFC 10015. The memo says these suites were removed from TLS 1.2.

today: RFC 5469 is Historic and was obsoleted by RFC 8996; it is also updated by RFC 10015.

sections.title: Two Older TLS Cipher Suites
sections.content: TLS versions 1.0 and 1.1 include cipher suites based on DES (Data Encryption Standard) and IDEA (International Data Encryption Algorithm). The RFC says single DES and IDEA are no longer recommended for general use in TLS and were removed from TLS 1.2. It records their definitions for completeness and explains why they should not be used.
sections.plainLanguage: The memo records two older encryption choices that appeared in earlier TLS versions. It explains why they should no longer be selected.

sections.title: DES and IDEA Cipher Properties
sections.content:
DES is treated as having a 64-bit key for TLS key generation, but only 56 bits provide protection because 8 bits are not used by the algorithm. DES uses 64-bit blocks. The RFC lists six DES cipher suites, all using CBC mode.

IDEA uses a 128-bit key and 64-bit blocks. The RFC defines one IDEA suite for TLS, TLS_RSA_WITH_IDEA_CBC_SHA.
sections.plainLanguage: DES provides 56 bits of protection despite its 64-bit key representation. IDEA uses a 128-bit key, but the RFC says its TLS suite was not widely used.

sections.title: Why the Suites Are Not Recommended
sections.content:
The RFC says practical brute-force attacks against DES had been known for over 20 years. It says TLS libraries should not implement single-DES suites; if a library does implement them, it should not enable them by default, and existing implementations should consider removing them.

The IDEA suite is not described as vulnerable to exhaustive key search, but the RFC says it was not widely used. Because rarely used code can cause security and interoperability problems, it says TLS libraries should not implement the suite and existing implementations should remove it. IANA updated the references for the already allocated suite values; the memo creates no new registry or assignment.
sections.plainLanguage: The RFC advises against single DES because it can be broken by trying keys. It also advises removing the IDEA suite because it was rarely used, which can make code harder to maintain safely.
